newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close lower on Greenspan jitters.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close lower on Greenspan jitters.

text.p: Argentina's bolsa closed lower Wednesday mimicking the slump on international markets after U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan warned of inflationary risks and surging stock prices, dealers said.
"The bolsa was nervous just like all the other markets because Greenspan's Senate testimony unleashed a selling wave in U.S. Treasuries," said Juan Napoli of brokers Ignoto y Napoli.
The blue-chip MerVal index clawed back from a session low of 734.83 to close at 742.36 with a loss of 1.4 percent.
The MerVal had shed 0.9 percent Tuesday after rallying 4.3 percent in the previous two sessions.

"Yesterday we saw a normal round of profit-taking which picked up speed today on Greenspan's statements. But I think this may have been a very good buying opportunity for some players who were waiting eagerly on the sidelines," said Npoli.
Floor volume swelled to an extremely heavy 48.9 million pesos from 42.5 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter deals shrank to 124.5 million pesos from 168.1 million Tuesday.
"With this volume and a price drop of just 1.4 percent, you can tell that people were buying, not just selling," another trader said.
He noted local economic fundamentals remained solid and said the bolsa had more short-term upside potential despite its steady advance in recent months.
The broad market pulled back 0.9 percent Wednesday, with losers whipping winners 43 to nine and 16 issues ending flat.
Heaviest main-tier losers were Bansud bank, Banco de Galicia and Telecom, which plummeted 3.6 percent, 3.1 percent and 2.9 percent, respectively.
The only MerVal gainers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, carmaker Sevel and shoemaker and textile firm Alpargatas, which tacked on 3.5 percent, 1.9 percent and 0.5 percent, respectively.
